title: moeb requires credential management for git and GitHub operations in conductor-driven context
description: When moeb runs interactively on a developer machine, git credentials (SSH key, GitHub token) are available from the user's configured environment. In a conductor-driven or containerised context, moeb must perform git commits, pushes, branch creation, and tagging without a human session. There is currently no mechanism in moeb to accept or securely use injected credentials for these operations. The conductor cannot drive moeb autonomously until this is resolved. Required credentials: (1) git SSH key or HTTPS token for push/pull/tag; (2) GitHub API token for PR creation, issue comment posting, release detection, and issue lifecycle updates. The credential surface must not appear in logs, signal files, run artefacts, or committed content.
proposed_resolution: 1. moeb should read git credentials from well-known environment variables (`MOEB_GIT_SSH_KEY_PATH`, `MOEB_GITHUB_TOKEN`) when present, falling back to the user's configured git credentials for interactive use. 2. The existing `.moeb/.secrets` file (already gitignored by init) should serve as an optional credential store for local non-interactive use, with documented key-value format. 3. Ensure all moeb tools that perform git or GitHub operations (`git_commit`, `create_branch`, `create_candidate_tag`, `github_releases`) respect the injected credentials and propagate them to git subprocesses via environment. 4. Document the expected environment variables in `.moeb/README.md`. 5. In the conductor's container deployment, credentials are injected via GitHub Actions secrets — moeb must not attempt interactive credential prompts when running non-interactively.
